messages:
maria: Hey team — Spectral Health wants a POC load run next Tue. They asked for a mixed-profile benchmark: 60% embeddings (<=128 tokens) + 40% generation (~512 tokens avg). Target: 250 qps sustained, handle 1k qps microbursts, and 95th gen latency <200ms, embeddings <50ms. KMS-enabled workspace. Can ops/SEs help size and confirm feasibility + rough pricing?

jon: I can take the lead on the run. Quick clarifying q's:
- Which deployment: Hosted API or Dedicated capacity?
- Model(s) to test (we have rdx-v2-large, rdx-quant-8b, and a gpt-compat baseline).
- Region preference (us-west-2 / eu-west-1)?

maria: They prefer Hosted to start (self-serve later), US-west-2. They asked us to include a quantized variant if it meets latency. Use rdx-v2-large + rdx-quant-8b fallback.

jon: OK. Plan I propose:
1) Smoke (5m): 10 qps, validate correctness + KMS passthrough.
2) Soak (30m): ramp to 250 qps sustained, measure p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rate.
3) Spike tests: run short 30s microbursts to 1k qps at steady-state to validate graceful degradation.
4) Variant comparison: run same profile on rdx-v2-large and rdx-quant-8b, compare 95th & token cost.

I'll use continuous-batching enabled, batch size auto, but cap max batch latency 12ms. We'll record CPU/GPU metrics and per-token cost.

ashwin: Notes from infra side: with Hosted + KMS you'll see encryption overhead on cold starts (~10-30ms) — recommend a ~10 minute warmup prior to soak. For the spike behavior, add a short TTL cache priming step (100 unique prefixes) so prefix cache doesn't distort results. Also confirm they want prefix/KV caching enabled (it impacts p95 heavily).

maria: Good call — they do want prefix caching enabled. Warmup OK. Also asked for a simple runbook they can read after — can we include a one-pager and the raw CSVs?

jon: Yep. I'll attach results + runbook. Draft run commands below (k6 + our SDK):

```
# k6 snippet (simplified)
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({model: 'rdx-v2-large', input: '...512 tokens prompt...', max_tokens: 512});
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${__ENV.TOKEN}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}});
  sleep(0.004); // ~250 rps/user
}
```

And an embeddings burst script will use shorter payloads with smaller token sizes.

elaine: Pricing note (quick rough): for hosted, estimate token-based cost + potential surge billing for microbursts. For the soak (30m @250qps, 40% gen @512 tokens avg): rough tokens = 30m*60s*250*(0.4*512 + 0.6*64) ~ ~23M tokens. Ballpark cost = tokens * hosted-rate (I'll pull exact numbers). If they opt for quant-8b we could reduce per-token cost by ~35%. I'll post a formal estimate once Jon confirms model run counts.

maria: Also security: they completed the initial questionnaire but flagged KMS provider (Azure KeyVault vs AWS KMS) + HSM requirement. Spectral prefers Azure KV. Is that supported for Hosted?

ashwin: Hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys via our tenant-level KMS bridge. Azure KV works but requires an inbound peering step and a short security review. HSM-level attestation is on the roadmap; for now we support HSM-backed keys only if customer provides them through a partner flow (ops-team assist). I'll add the security checklist to the runbook.

jon: Scheduling: I have a slot Wed 09:30 PT for pre-run checks, Tue for the actual run. deploy-bot, can you reserve the perf-run slot and spin up a temp test tenant with KMS linked?

deploy-bot: Scheduled: perf-run-precheck @1769463600 (Wed 09:30 PT). Bench run scheduled: 1769550000 (Tue). Temp tenant created: spectral-poc-temp-1729. KMS link pending (manual step by infra). :white_check_mark:

maria: Awesome. Jon — can you also capture cool-down behavior and tail-latency heatmaps? They care about p99+ spikes. Keep the results CSVs and a summarized slide (1-2 pages) for AE review.

jon: Will do. Next steps:
- Jon: build the k6 scenarios + run templates (today).
- Ashwin: confirm KMS onboarding checklist + warmup script (today).
- Elaine: formal cost estimate and pricing note (EOD).
- Maria: confirm that Spectral is OK with Wed precheck and share any special compliance asks.

maria: Confirmed with Spectral — Wed precheck good. They asked to include a short latency vs concurrency curve in the deliverable.

jon: Noted. I'll attach the final runbook and results to this thread after the run. :thumbsup:
